trust_decision.summary: Which database namespace the model's Queryable Encryption schema is keyed to in EncryptedFieldsMap (decided in MongoClientSettingsHelper.CreateSettings from options.DatabaseName only); a null name yields '.Coll' keys that match no collection, so declared-encrypted fields are stored as plaintext. NOTE: this does not match the advisory's CWE-532 'logs' summary.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary ('Logs may collect sensitive information', CWE-532) leads to the LogFragment builder, which the pinned commit's own HEAD commit (EF-384/386) already changed to stop logging the connection string; the published fix touches a different file entirely.

fix_sites.entry_point: Public API: DbContextOptionsBuilder.UseMongoDB(connectionString) + a model with QE-encrypted properties, on first DbContext use (MongoClientWrapper.Client)
Same; new guard throws when no database name can be resolved and a QE schema exists

fix_sites.module_kind: storage wrapper (second copy of database-name resolution)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/MongoDB.EntityFrameworkCore/Storage/MongoClientWrapper.cs:156-167 (correct db-name resolution, incl. connection-string path, lives here and is not shared with MongoClientSettingsHelper.cs:77)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: MongoClientWrapper already resolves the database name from the connection string correctly, so a solver who only looks there concludes resolution is fine and misses that CreateSettings re-derives it from options.DatabaseName alone.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Contexts configured with a pre-built ClientSettings/connection string and no QE schema (or QueryableEncryptionSchemaMode.Ignore) must keep working without a database name in CreateSettings; an over-broad 'throw when no database name' breaks them. Also existing user-supplied EncryptedFieldsMap entries must be preserved by the merge.

O6_input_shapes: database name only in connection-string path (mongodb://host/db)
connection string with no path / trailing slash only (must throw when QE schema present)
ClientSettings without DatabaseName (null name, must throw when QE schema present)
malformed connection string (wrapper previously swallowed FormatException)

O7_producer.where: src/MongoDB.EntityFrameworkCore/Storage/MongoClientWrapper.cs:156-167 (database name derived from options/connection string); schema from src/MongoDB.EntityFrameworkCore/Infrastructure/QueryableEncryptionSchemaProvider.cs:26-27

O8b_injection_room.sibling: EnsureCreated could create QE collections with encryptedFields keyed by a separately derived database name
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The creator already creates collections per root entity type via clientWrapper.Database; a maintainer adding explicit encrypted-collection creation would plausibly re-derive the namespace locally.

O9_family: Missing encryption of sensitive data (CWE-311/312 style: declared-encrypted fields silently stored as plaintext); advisory metadata claims CWE-532 log exposure, which the diff does not address

O10_build.toolchain: .NET SDK (net8.0 / net10.0 targets), MongoDB.Driver 3.11.2 via NuGet
O10_build.project_tests: tests/MongoDB.EntityFrameworkCore.UnitTests/Infrastructure/MongoClientSettingsHelperTests.cs (unit, no server; CreateSettings only builds settings). Full QE end-to-end needs mongod + crypt_shared, not required for unit-level scoring.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Pass the wrapper's already-resolved _databaseName into CreateSettings (or keep options?.DatabaseName) without adding the null-name guard for ClientSettings/no-path connection strings.

out_of_scope_notes: Advisory/diff mismatch: CVE summary and CWE-532 describe log exposure, but fix dec7e26 (EF-389) is a Queryable Encryption namespace-keying fix; the actual connection-string logging fix appears to be the pinned commit itself (ef6f222, EF-384/386), already reflected at src/MongoDB.EntityFrameworkCore/Infrastructure/MongoOptionsExtension.cs:311-312.

CreateLogFragment still appends Extension.ClientSettings via ToString (src/MongoDB.EntityFrameworkCore/Infrastructure/MongoOptionsExtension.cs:319-322); whether the driver's MongoClientSettings.ToString exposes credentials was not checked.
Total sites are effectively one decision (namespace keying) in one helper; the wrapper change is a refactor to share resolution.
